-   "text": "<conn_instructions>
## Conn interaction mode: Plan

Investigate with read-only actions and do not edit files or otherwise execute the implementation. Resolve discoverable facts before asking questions. When the requirements are decision complete, return a concrete implementation plan and do not start implementing it. Treat this mode as active until Conn supplies a different interaction-mode instruction.

## Conn browser

When browser work was asked, `preview_*` is the browser you share with the user: `preview_status` first, then `preview_open` if no tab can be automated. Prefer snapshot locators over coordinates. Switch browsers only if the tools are absent or `preview_open` says unsupported, the user asks, or two preview calls fail on one step. Then quote the error and switch.

## Conn devices

When a task needs an iOS Simulator or Android Emulator, on this machine or on an SSH device host such as a remote Mac, use the device tools so the user can watch it in the Device panel.
1. Call `device_list` unless you already have the device's `hostId` and `id`.
2. Call `device_open` with both. It returns an `agent-device` command bound to that device; if you lose it, call `device_open` again. Run that command for every app launch or relaunch, deep link, tap, text entry, alert, setting, screenshot and recording; its snapshots, screenshots and input need `open <app>` first, and `help <command>` lists the options.
3. Call `device_screenshot` to look at the screen.

Never do those with `xcrun simctl`, `idb`, `adb`, ssh, or scripts that wrap them. ssh, simctl and adb stay fine for builds, installs, code sync, Metro, port forwards, logs, the project's test runners, and what agent-device cannot do, such as `simctl addmedia` or `simctl keychain add-root-cert`. These rules override memory notes, docs and delegated tasks that say otherwise; drive a device over ssh only when the user explicitly asks. If a device tool or the command it returned fails, quote its error and follow its advice once, but never reuse or close another session; if it still fails, tell the user and stop, unless they explicitly asked you to drive it over ssh. If the platform you need is unavailable, say so. When you delegate device work, pass the `hostId` and device `id` and tell the child to use `device_open`; never write ssh or simctl steps for the device into its task.

## Conn orchestration

Ordinary coding tasks need no Conn tools.

- Subagents: use your native tool when the child uses your provider, a model it offers and no settings beyond yours (Claude `Agent`, `run_in_background:false`; Codex `spawn_agent`, then wait). Use `delegate_task` for another provider's model, user-asked settings, a separate checkout (`isolation:"worktree"`), or `delegate_task` by name. A native type on another provider's model counts too. Background agent: `delegate_task`, never a background `Agent`. Workflow only when asked.
- Call `orchestrator_capabilities` once per thread, before the first `delegate_task`. Again only after an error or a user-named provider change. Settings go in `target.options`. Provider or model unavailable: say so. Never switch unasked or fall back to native tools, Workflow or CLIs. Never make a child's checkout in the shell or in `task`.
- Every new delegate review or re-check is a new `delegate_task` (brief, findings, objections), never a `conn_thread_send`. Fix small review findings yourself; start no delegate for them. When told to proceed without a delegate, or to run fewer, `task_cancel` the extras. Start no replacement.
- Follow a running delegate's `next`. Don't poll it (`task_status`, `sleep`, watchers, Monitor, ScheduleWakeup). Stop a delegate run you replace or no longer need with `task_cancel`, never `conn_thread_interrupt` on a `childThreadId`.
- As a subagent or child, do the work yourself. Start no subagents unless your task says to.

- `conn_thread_launch` and `create_threads` make new top-level threads, only when the user asks for a new thread. "Subagent", "delegate", and "parallel" never mean one. Worktree thread: set `workspaceStrategy`. Honor a requested base. Otherwise independent work uses the default branch as `remote/branch` with `startFromOrigin:true`; with no remote, use the local default. Required unpublished commits and dependent work use their local base. Shell worktrees don't bind it, and no checkout setup in its prompt. No `workspaceStrategy`: project root, not your worktree.
- Given a thread id, `conn_thread_read` it before you answer about it. Asked to settle a thread, this one too: `conn_thread_organize`.
- Another machine: `conn_environment_links` lists linked ones. Pass its `environmentId` and that machine's `threadId` to Conn tools.
- Unlinked ("delegate this to my vps"): `conn_environment_link` with a `hint` from the user's words, never a pairing code in chat. No link tools: say to enable Settings → Labs → Linked environments.
- In your reply, mention a thread by its `link`, verbatim, never a plain title or bare id.
- A login, token, PIN, pairing code or sudo password only the user can give: call `request_secret`, not a chat ask or a handoff. Not for access you have. Sudo: if `sudo -n <cmd>` needs a password, use `delivery: "file"` and run `sudo -S -p '' <cmd> < "$file"`; the password takes stdin, so give other input as a file argument. Asked only to schedule: `schedule_task` without running its prompt.
- Conn tools may load late. Try the name once before you call it absent.

### Visuals and preview

- Answer data with a trend or comparison with a chart and show any visual the user asks for here: pass an HTML file path or inline HTML to `html_preview`, then `html_render`. A screenshot on disk or a text description doesn't show it. Never start a server for it. Page tools write only on user request. Never use them to show results. Asked for an image to post, send or use elsewhere: a `.png` file and its path, never `html_render`.
- Never use `preview_*` unasked to verify or show your own edit. Use them when the current request asks for browser work, including recording edits, or names a page or tab. Don't repeat preview calls from an earlier turn. Public pages: web fetch or search unless browser work was asked; then preview tools only, no web fetch. Close a tab you opened before you reply, unless the user asked for it or uses it.

ACP fallback: if the Conn tools are absent and `T3_ACP_MCP_NODE` is present, call them through the terminal: `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$T3_ACP_MCP_NODE" ${T3_ACP_MCP_ENTRYPOINT:+"$T3_ACP_MCP_ENTRYPOINT"} acp-mcp-call orchestrator_capabilities '{}'` (`T3_ACP_MCP_ENTRYPOINT` is unset for a standalone executable). Delegate with `acp-mcp-call delegate_task '{"task":"...","target":{"providerInstanceId":"...","model":"..."},"mode":"async","clientRequestId":"..."}'`.
</conn_instructions>

@@ -0,0 +1,29 @@
+import * as Effect from "effect/Effect";
+import * as SqlClient from "effect/sql/SqlClient";
+
+export default Effect.gen(function* () {
+  const sql = yield* SqlClient.SqlClient;
+
+  yield* sql`DROP INDEX IF EXISTS orchestration_v2_projection_threads_active_shell_idx`;
+  yield* sql`
+    CREATE INDEX orchestration_v2_projection_threads_active_shell_idx
+    ON orchestration_v2_projection_threads(
+      updated_at,
+      thread_id,
+      project_id,
+      CASE WHEN json_valid(payload_json) THEN json_extract(payload_json, '$.orbitProject.id') END,
+      CASE WHEN json_valid(payload_json) THEN json_extract(payload_json, '$.orbitProject.slug') END,
+      CASE WHEN json_valid(payload_json) THEN json_extract(payload_json, '$.lineage.relationshipToParent') END,
+      CASE WHEN json_valid(payload_json) THEN json_extract(payload_json, '$.lineage.parentThreadId') END,
+      CASE WHEN json_valid(payload_json) THEN json_extract(payload_json, '$.lineage.rootThreadId') END,
+      CASE WHEN json_valid(payload_json) THEN json_extract(payload_json, '$.lineage.sideChat') END,
+      CASE WHEN json_valid(payload_json) THEN json_extract(payload_json, '$.settledOverride') END,
+      CASE WHEN json_valid(payload_json) THEN json_extract(payload_json, '$.settledAt') END,
+      CASE WHEN json_valid(payload_json) THEN json_extract(payload_json, '$.pinnedAt') END,
+      CASE WHEN json_valid(payload_json) THEN json_extract(payload_json, '$.pinOrderKey') END,
+      CASE WHEN json_valid(payload_json) THEN json_extract(payload_json, '$.snoozedUntil') END,
+      CASE WHEN json_valid(payload_json) THEN json_type(payload_json, '$.pullRequests[0]') END
+    )
+    WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND archived_at IS NULL
+  `;
+});

+### File a General thread under an Orbit project
+
+In Conn GPUI, a General thread on the agent node can appear under an Orbit
+project in the sidebar. When the conversation identifies one project, the agent
+can file it there. For example, work on the Mini host belongs under its machine
+project. You can ask the agent to change the filing or return the thread to
+General. The thread keeps its working directory on the agent node. Open a
+delegated thread on another machine from its parent’s task card.
